findings.title: Attaching or removing references on a saved project is lost on Save — persistence uses the last synthesis's stale reference list
findings.surface: Attach reference / remove chip → Save → reopen
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts an Editor attaching a file after synthesis then saving sees the chip disappear on reopening. Conversely removing a reference and saving restores the removed chip on reopening, and a later regeneration sends that reference again. Uploading the object with a project id does not fix the issue because project reopening never discovers attached references from the file collection. Regenerating before Save is a costly, undisclosed workaround.
findings.expected: R-078: "each attached reference ... stays attached to the project for later regenerations"; request: "Each can be removed individually." Saving must persist the currently chosen reference list without requiring another paid synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Open a generated saved project.
Attach a new reference (or remove an existing reference chip).
Press Save without synthesizing again.
Reopen the project; the old reference list returns.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:156 maintains references separately; :189 copies them into result.context only when generation completes. :263-265 splitResult returns result.context unchanged; :270-274 saves that context. Files.jsx:43 and :61 update only the separate references state. openSystem at Workspace.jsx:298 restores context.references.

findings.title: Reloading or deep-linking a cloud project opens the default workspace — project identity is never retained in the URL
findings.surface: /projects/{id}; project open and page reload
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts opening /projects/<id> renders an unsaved default workspace, and reloading after opening a cloud project loses the selected project and inputs. Users must find it in Projects again; browser back/forward cannot return between project selections. Saved data remains recoverable through the list.
findings.expected: R-113: "Opening /projects/{id} directly ... loads that project's saved system ... and a reload keeps the same project open"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "direct access, reload, back and return paths" must retain the referenced object.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing project from Projects.
Reload the page: the workspace initializes with no project.
Open /projects/<that id> in a fresh signed-in tab.
The catch-all renders the default workspace without loading the id.
findings.evidence: App.js:27 routes every otherwise unmatched path to Workspace without extracting a project id. Workspace.jsx:168 only reads a ?project query; :171 immediately replaces even that URL with '/'. :305-311 opens project state without changing the URL.

findings.title: Accepted reference code and PDF content is silently omitted — extraction truncates at 20,000 characters and 40 pages
findings.surface: Attach reference → Synthesize
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts an accepted 30 KB .h whose class declaration lies after a long license/comment prefix loses that entire declaration before generation, and a PDF's page 41 is never considered. The chip still shows a successful attachment and the full file is stored, so developers pay for a synthesis that cannot follow the omitted specification without knowing to split/rewrite it. UTF-8 text and PDF extraction do reach Claude for content inside those silent bounds.
findings.expected: R-104 and request: "AI uses them as source material", e.g. "extend this existing header"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Compare complete intended content and actual input selection" and make skipped input visible. Within the stated 10 MB acceptance limit, required content must reach the model or limitations must be communicated before synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid UTF-8 header under 10 MB with the declared class after character 20,000 (or a spec with requirements on PDF page 41).
Ask to extend that class or implement that requirement and Synthesize.
The model prompt receives only the truncated prefix.
No attachment or generation UI reports that the required content was omitted.
findings.evidence: projects.py:22 sets TEXT_CHARS=20000; :261 takes PDF pages[:40] then text[:TEXT_CHARS]; :265 truncates decoded code/text to 20000 characters. :299-304 stores the full original size and reports successful attachment without a truncation flag. server.py:230-232 sends only that extracted text.

findings.title: Abandoned synthesis keeps polling after navigation or sign-out — async polling has no lifecycle cancellation
findings.surface: Running synthesis → leave workspace/sign out
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts signing out or navigating to a public share view during generation leaves the old polling loop alive for up to five minutes, issuing requests and (after sign-out) refresh attempts. Returning and starting another run adds a separate loop; old completions still issue progress/result callbacks and success toasts. The UI cannot cancel the abandoned loop. Normal completion does stop its loop.
findings.expected: R-118: polling "stops ... when ... user leaves the workspace"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "polling ends with its owner". Leaving a workspace must terminate its client polling and callbacks.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize on a slow job.
Sign out or navigate within the app to another routed surface before it finishes.
Return to the workspace and start another generation.
The first loop has no cleanup and keeps polling alongside the new one until its deadline/completion.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:43-50 loops with a new setTimeout and GET every two seconds until five minutes, done or error; there is no AbortSignal or mounted guard. Workspace's only effect at :164-174 returns no synthesis cleanup. AuthContext.jsx:31-33 can unmount Workspace on sign-out. The polling catch at Workspace.jsx:48-49 also ignores permanent 401/404.

findings.title: Keyboard focus escapes modal dialogs into covered workspace actions — modal primitive supplies no focus management
findings.surface: Share, reset-link, migration and conflict modals
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts keyboard users opening Share remain focused on the background Share button and can Tab through covered Copy, Export, Save, description and project controls before reaching modal fields. They can invoke covered actions while a supposedly modal share/reset/conflict surface is open. Closing does not restore focus. Pointer users can use the modal normally; keyboard users must traverse unrelated controls and risk acting on background work.
findings.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus stays visible and follows the active surface" and "Dialog close ... restores ... focus". Modal keyboard interaction must stay on the dialog rather than reaching covered workspace controls.
reproduction_steps: Focus the workspace Share button using the keyboard and press Enter.
Press Tab repeatedly.
Focus is not moved into or contained by the Share dialog, so background controls remain in the tab order.
Close the modal with Escape; no focus restoration is performed.
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 only installs Escape; :11-12 renders aria-modal dialog/backdrop, but has no focus assignment, focus trap, background inertness or restore-focus logic. ShareModal.jsx:46 uses this primitive while Workspace's editing actions remain mounted; AccountMenu.jsx:19 uses it for admin reset.

findings.title: Files with non-Latin filenames cannot be downloaded — raw Unicode is placed into a latin-1 HTTP header
findings.surface: Files → Download; GET /api/files/{file_id}
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts uploading a valid file named '角色设计.txt' succeeds, but downloading it raises UnicodeEncodeError while constructing the response headers because those characters cannot be encoded as latin-1. A teammate/viewer receives a failed download instead of any bytes. An uploader could rename and re-upload outside the app, but recipients cannot fix the stored name themselves.
findings.expected: R-080/R-081: downloading returns "original name and identical bytes"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: preserve "encoding ... filename". A valid Unicode filename must not prevent delivery; use an encoded filename* with a safe fallback.
reproduction_steps: Upload a small project file named 角色设计.txt.
Open Files as a member and press Download.
The download endpoint attempts to place that raw name in its response header and fails before delivering the file.
findings.evidence: projects.py:281 preserves arbitrary original filenames; :330 removes only double quotes and :331 interpolates the name directly into the Content-Disposition header of starlette Response. requirements.txt pins starlette 0.37.2; header values use HTTP latin-1 encoding rather than Unicode filename* encoding. Files.jsx:19 needs that GET to succeed before creating a blob download.

findings.title: Compare hides parameter/module/note edits and misstates old module selection — it discards those input changes and snapshots edited state
findings.surface: Compare → Input changes and Parameters & Modules
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a regeneration changing Max Health, toggling StaminaDrain and adding notes opens Compare with no corresponding Input changes chips. Its Parameters & Modules view also uses the already-toggled old module state, so a module removal can show no before/after module difference. Code/text line diff still works, but users cannot reliably audit which requested edits produced it.
findings.expected: R-094: Compare "lists which inputs changed" across "parameters and modules"; request: "see the effect of dial or prompt changes"; R-086 includes parameter values, module toggles/additions and notes. Compare's previous side and changed-input list must reflect the actual previous synthesis, not edited chips.
reproduction_steps: Generate a system with a parameter and an enabled module.
Change that parameter, toggle the module off, add notes and Synthesize.
Inspect Compare's Input changes: those edits are omitted.
Switch to Parameters & Modules: the previous module is already off, hiding the actual toggle.
findings.evidence: CompareView.jsx:34 passes params:{} and notes:"" to computeChanges and :35 removes every module change. Workspace.jsx:248-254 mutates result.modules before regeneration; :188 sets that already-edited result as previousResult. computeChanges (changes.js:27-40) only detects params/notes when supplied and needs original module state.

findings.title: Cloud projects lose their before/after comparison on reopening — only the current synthesis is persisted
findings.surface: Saved cloud project → Compare
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts a developer synthesizing twice, comparing and saving a cloud project loses the previous side after reload/reopen. Another Editor opening that saved project cannot inspect the changes at all. They must pay for another regeneration just to create a new pair, and the original comparison cannot be reconstructed through the app because the previous output was discarded.
findings.expected: R-095's independently checkable outcome is retrieval of previous/current sections for a cloud project; request: "Stack Systems and Compare keep working with cloud projects" and Phase 2 adds "any earlier version, not just the last one." Phase 1 should retain the immediate before/after comparison across save and reopen, without requiring full Phase 2 history or a particular API route.
reproduction_steps: Generate, tune and regenerate a system, then inspect Compare.
Save the project and reopen it (or open it on another device).
Open Compare: only the empty 'Synthesize twice' message is available.
No saved previous synthesis or changed-input record can be loaded.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:152 previousResult is only React state; :188 assigns it after an in-session run. splitResult :263-265 exports/saves result only, with no previousResult. openSystem :300 explicitly clears previousResult. backend/projects.py:127-132 stores only current system/context; :169-172 replaces them on save. CompareView.jsx:44-49 then shows 'Synthesize twice'.

findings.title: Retrying browser migration duplicates saved systems — every import mints a fresh project with no legacy identity
findings.surface: First-sign-in browser migration → Import them
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts clicking Import them twice while migration is in progress or retrying its request duplicates each legacy system under fresh ids. The modal remains actionable throughout and the backend has no idempotency key. The user's cloud library becomes cluttered with duplicate projects; manual deletion is the safe recovery.
findings.expected: R-085: posting the same browser library twice "creates no duplicate project"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record/operation/effect identity ... retries ... concurrent creation." A given browser-saved system imported by one migration intent must create one cloud copy, while distinct legacy systems remain distinct.
reproduction_steps: Have multiple systems in the old browser library and sign in for the first time.
Click Import them twice before the first network loop finishes (or retry the same import payload).
Both loops POST the same entries.
Mine contains separately identified duplicates of each imported system.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:330-334 posts every migration item to /projects/import and the Import them button at :752 has no busy guard. projects.py:152 calls create each time; :128 mints a new project_id and :133 inserts without a legacy-source identity check. server.py:42-49 has no owner/legacy-id uniqueness index.

findings.title: Failed browser migrations cannot be retried in the app — failures are swallowed and the one-time prompt is marked complete
findings.surface: Browser migration partial-failure path
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a transient network/storage failure during first migration leaves some or all systems unimported, then permanently suppresses the offer and labels the operation with a success toast. The raw legacy data remains in localStorage, but the new cloud-only library has no control to reopen or retry that browser library, so the user cannot recover through the intended UI without developer/storage intervention.
findings.expected: R-084: "Import creates one project per browser system"; request: "Import them copies them into the account"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Walk failure boundaries for batches ... visible rejected/skipped input". Partial failures must be explained and retryable rather than marking unfinished migration complete.
reproduction_steps: Start first-sign-in Import them with legacy systems present.
Have one or more POST /projects/import requests fail (e.g. a transient network interruption).
After the loop the modal closes and reports Imported N of M.
Reload: the completion marker prevents another migration offer despite the missing projects.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:334 swallows every failed per-item import; :336 emits a success toast even for zero imported; :339 writes the migration-completed key regardless of failures and :340 closes the modal. Initialization at :166-167 offers migration only if that key is absent. Browser data is not removed, but no retry UI exists.

findings.title: Double-clicking Save project creates duplicate cloud projects — initial save has no pending guard or operation identity
findings.surface: Save project; POST /api/projects
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer double-clicking Save project on an unsaved synthesis gets two distinct cloud projects. The UI provides no pending state and both calls show success. Manual deletion is a safe but unnecessary cleanup; this is separate from migration duplication because normal saves use a different entry point and have no migration source id.
findings.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls and server-side operation identity preserve one create ... per intent"; request: "Save ... work as they do today, but in the cloud." Repeated clicks during a single initial Save should create one project.
reproduction_steps: Generate an unsaved system.
Click Save project twice before the first request returns.
Both captured calls choose POST /projects.
Projects → Mine contains two copies of the same initial save.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:418 Save is disabled only when !result or readOnly, not while saving. :272-274 uses captured project state; before the first POST resolves, a second call still sees project null and POSTs again. projects.py:128/133 always mints and inserts another project, with no create operation identity.

findings.title: Malformed imported project JSON crashes the workspace after being saved — importer validates only system_name
findings.surface: Projects → Import; POST /api/projects/import
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts importing valid JSON with a system_name but tunable_parameters set to a string (or non-array modules) stores the record and then causes an uncaught frontend TypeError when ProjectsPanel opens it. The workspace becomes unusable rather than explaining the invalid file. Reload resets the open project, allowing the user to delete the broken row; ordinary valid exports do round-trip system/context correctly.
findings.expected: Checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "malformed/partial input ... visible rejected/skipped input"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "fields, types" must match at both ends; R-082/R-083 promise usable project import. Malformed project JSON must be refused without storing a broken project or crashing the workspace.
reproduction_steps: Use Import project with a JSON object containing system_name 'Broken' and tunable_parameters 'bad'.
The server accepts it because system_name is truthy.
The import UI immediately opens it.
Workspace's forEach/map assumptions throw instead of showing an import-validation message.
findings.evidence: projects.py:125 checks only truthy system_name; :147 accepts the whole imported dict as a system and :151-152 stores it without SystemOutput validation. Workspace.jsx:299 renders it, :362 calls tunable_parameters.forEach and :659 calls modules.map. No error boundary is present in App.js:32-40.

findings.title: Incomplete or unhonored generations are reported as successful — output validation checks types but not required content or edit coverage
findings.surface: Claude response → completed synthesis and Applied in this synthesis
findings.observed: AI and model features: source proves that if Claude returns a JSON object with all required keys but empty code, empty graph/setup lists, no applied_changes, or a tunable value different from an explicit override, the backend records done and the UI announces success. A user requesting Max Health=250 can receive and save a 100-valued output, with no row explaining that edit; empty output is also accepted. This is a conditional source trace of an accepted bad provider reply, not an observed model failure. Users must manually audit/retry paid generations instead of trusting the promised feedback.
findings.expected: R-087: "one applied entry per queued change"; R-089: why notes explain setup decisions; R-097: non-empty complete code/graph/setup; R-102: requested values are used. Checklist, AI and model features: "parsing, semantic validation ... empty/malformed results ... to the user-visible outcome." A structurally valid but incomplete/unapplied reply must not be confirmed as completed synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Queue a parameter change and a designer note, then Synthesize.
Consider a provider reply with the expected field types but applied_changes omitted and tunable value unchanged (or empty code/graph lists).
SystemOutput validation accepts it and marks the job done.
The UI shows success and hides the missing change report rather than rejecting/reconciling the incomplete result.
findings.evidence: server.py:128 makes setup why optional with default ''; :150 defaults applied_changes to []; :143-148 accepts empty code strings and empty graph/setup lists. :303 performs only SystemOutput(**data), then :308 marks done. There is no comparison against req.change_requests, req.parameter_overrides or required output completeness. ChangePanels.jsx:36-38 hides the panel entirely when changes are absent.

findings.title: One reset link can change the password twice concurrently — token consumption happens after an unguarded password write
findings.surface: POST /api/auth/reset-password; reset link redemption
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two concurrent requests with the same reset link and different new passwords can both observe used=False and both report success, with the second password winning. The first user is then unable to sign in with the password the screen confirmed. A person retaining the same reset URL can race a legitimate redemption; another admin reset link is needed to recover safely.
findings.expected: R-059: the reset token is "single-use" and "a second use ... is refused"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations" must preserve effect identity under concurrent requests. Only one password change may succeed for a given token.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a fresh on-screen reset link.
Submit that token concurrently from two clients with different valid new passwords, before either marks it used.
Both requests can pass the unused check and update the password.
Only the last password works despite both submissions reporting success.
findings.evidence: auth.py:229 reads a reset record; :230 checks used; :232 changes the password; only afterward :233 sets used=True using a token-only filter. There is no atomic used=False claim or transaction before the password write. ResetPassword in AuthPages.jsx:42-58 has no busy guard against overlapping submissions.

findings.title: Google-first users cannot add email/password sign-in themselves — registration rejects their email and no password-linking flow exists
findings.surface: Google-first account → email registration/sign-in
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Google-first user trying Create account with the same email is refused, and Sign in with email always fails because no password exists. They can continue using Google, but cannot add the promised second method without owner-assisted password reset, which is not an ordinary self-service linking flow.
findings.expected: R-055: "Signing in with Google ... and later registering with email/password ... reaches one account"; request: "Two ways to sign in ... If both use the same email address, they reach the same account." Provide a secure authenticated way to add the password method to the existing account, without creating a duplicate.
reproduction_steps: Sign in for the first time using Google and save a project.
Sign out and choose Create account with the same email and a password.
Registration says the account already exists.
Try email Sign in: the Google-first record has no password, and there is no account control to set one.
findings.evidence: auth.py:174-178 creates Google-first users without password_hash. :128-129 rejects every registration for an existing email; :148 rejects email sign-in when password_hash is missing. No set-password/account-link action exists in AccountMenu.jsx:58-65; only an admin can issue a reset link (:214-224).

findings.title: Older projects and files silently disappear from their lists — fixed 500-record caps have no pagination or truncation notice
findings.surface: Projects lists and Files tab at more than 500 records
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that once a user has 501 live owned projects (including repeated imports) their oldest project disappears from Mine and the count reads 500, with no way to load the remaining page. Likewise a project's 501st-oldest file is omitted from Files. Records are still stored and retrievable if an id was retained, but ordinary users cannot discover/download older work through the UI on a new device.
findings.expected: Request: cloud Projects "saved safely and available on any device" and Files keeps project artifacts; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation" and "counts ... match the rows they summarize." All stored accessible projects/files must remain discoverable as the library grows.
reproduction_steps: Accumulate or import 501 distinct projects in one account.
Open Projects → Mine; only the newest 500 appear with count 500.
Look for the oldest project or a next-page control: neither is available.
The same cutoff applies after uploading more than 500 project files.
findings.evidence: projects.py:113/:117 use to_list(500) with no skip/cursor/total; :322 also caps file listing at 500. ProjectsPanel.jsx:71 labels lists[id].length as the count and :86 renders only those rows, with no paging/Load more action. ProjectFiles similarly renders the returned files only (:119).

findings.title: Image-only PDFs are accepted but invisible to Claude — PDF processing extracts text only and sends no visual pages
findings.surface: PDF reference attachment → Synthesize
findings.observed: AI and model features: source predicts a scanned spec or PDF containing a UI screenshot but no text layer uploads successfully yet supplies an empty body to Claude. No PDF bytes or rendered page images reach the model and no empty-extraction warning appears. The designer's request to match that PDF cannot be grounded in its actual content; converting it manually to an image is a safe workaround once the limitation is discovered.
findings.expected: Request: "Accepted types are screenshots and images, PDFs" and "The AI uses them as source material"; R-104; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: trace "complete intended content and actual input selection". A valid PDF whose content is graphical must reach the model visually or be explicitly rejected/warned, not silently treated as empty source.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid image-only PDF under 10 MB containing the desired UI/spec.
Ask Synthesize to follow it.
extract_text returns empty text and no image_bytes are generated for application/pdf.
The model request contains the filename but none of the PDF's visible source content.
findings.evidence: projects.py:261 uses only PdfReader page.extract_text() for PDF references. upload_file :294-295 calls it for any non-image reference; load_references :347-349 attaches image_bytes only when content_type starts image/. server.py:230 sends extracted PDF text, while :285 includes only image_bytes as visual content.

findings.title: Notes typed while a synthesis is running disappear on completion — the old request unconditionally clears the live draft
findings.surface: Notes for next synthesis during a running generation
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer entering new notes for the next pass while Claude is generating loses those notes when the old request completes. They were not in that request's body, are not in result.context, and are erased from the visible field with no warning. Rewriting the short draft is the only recovery; controls suggest editing remains allowed during generation.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: input and operation state must remain coherent. R-086/request: notes before the next Synthesize must be injected rather than silently discarded.
reproduction_steps: Start a synthesis or regeneration.
While it is running, type a new note such as 'use a Gameplay Tag for stun' in Notes for next synthesis.
Wait for the current job to complete.
The new note disappears although it was never sent to that job or saved in its context.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:187 awaits the long-running job; :189 snapshots the notes submitted at start; :190 unconditionally clears the live notes state on completion. The notes textarea at :702-710 is inside a fieldset disabled only by readOnly (:608), not loading, so users can keep editing notes while the job runs.

findings.title: Reloading strands the paid synthesis result — the only job handle exists inside the old polling call
findings.surface: Running background synthesis → browser reload
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts reloading during a generation loses the job id and returns to an idle workspace even though the server keeps generating and spending the owner's credits. The completed result remains in Mongo but is unreachable through any workspace/library action; only someone who retained the API id can retrieve it. The ordinary UI recovery is to pay for another synthesis. Normal uninterrupted polling delivers the result.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "interruption ... revisit ... resume ... retrieves the completed session" where supported; users rely on: "A paid background synthesis can be retrieved after an ordinary page reload rather than requiring a second paid run." R-099/R-100 describe server background generation and delivery of its finished system.
reproduction_steps: Press Synthesize and wait until the background job has started.
Reload the browser before it finishes.
The new workspace starts idle with no resume/recent-job control.
Allow the original job to finish: it is not shown or recoverable in Projects unless the original page had saved its result.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:36-38 keeps job_id only in a local async variable; no component/localStorage/project field stores it and mount at :164-174 loads only templates/migration/query project. server.py:315-318 persists jobs but only :325-330 GET-by-id retrieves them; there is no current/recent job lookup or result recovery consumer.

findings.title: Oversized uploads can exhaust worker memory before rejection — file limits are checked only after an unbounded read
findings.surface: POST /api/files oversized uploads
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts a signed-in user's oversized 1 GB upload is fully read into a bytes object before its eventual 413, and concurrent such uploads multiply the allocation. The documented 25 MB ceiling therefore does not bound worker memory, risking interruptions to other users' saves/generations under a reachable large-upload workload. No runtime memory/latency measurement was made; exact failure depends on deployment memory.
findings.expected: Request: "10 MB per reference file and 25 MB per project file"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "buffering ... bounds and backpressure" must prevent material resource growth for reachable input. Oversized uploads must be rejected without unbounded application-memory buffering.
reproduction_steps: As a member with Editor access, upload a project file much larger than 25 MB.
The endpoint reads the full file into memory first.
Only after that allocation does it return the size-limit error.
Concurrent oversized uploads repeat that full allocation per request.
findings.evidence: projects.py:284 executes data = await file.read() without a size bound, then :285-287 applies 10/25 MB limits using len(data). The multipart UploadFile may be disk-spooled, but this call materializes the entire uploaded body in application memory before rejection.

findings.title: Admin reset-link creation stops working after access-token expiry — refresh interceptor skips protected auth routes
findings.surface: Account menu → Password reset link → Create
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an email-signed-in admin waiting over 15 minutes then choosing Password reset link receives 'Not authenticated' on Create, repeatedly, despite the still-valid refresh session. Other project API calls refresh automatically, but this action never does. Reloading or forcing an unrelated project request restores it; this is bounded but confusing account-management failure.
findings.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Trace token storage ... expiry ... refresh/retry where refresh tokens exist"; R-058: admin can create an on-screen reset link. An active admin with a valid refresh session must not need unrelated navigation or reload for this protected account action.
reproduction_steps: Sign in as admin using email/password.
Wait beyond the 15-minute access-token lifetime without making a refreshing API call.
Open Account menu → Password reset link and press Create for a valid user.
The /auth/ exclusion prevents refresh, so Create fails until reload or another non-auth API call renews access.
findings.evidence: api.js:11 excludes every URL beginning /auth/ from refresh/retry. AccountMenu.jsx:14 posts /auth/admin/reset-link, whose backend Depends(admin_user) calls current_user and returns 401 after the 15-minute access expiry (auth.py:16,86-96). The refresh cookie remains valid seven days (:17,42).

findings.title: Viewer project regeneration is restricted only in the UI — generation requests have no enforced project identity or Editor check
findings.surface: POST /api/generate project regeneration
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Viewer sending a project regeneration directly can start a paid Claude job and obtain its revised output because project identity is ignored, whereas the UI says regeneration requires Editor access. Saving back to the shared project is correctly refused, so this is a bounded generation-role violation rather than unauthorized durable project mutation. The endpoint must distinguish an allowed new personal synthesis from a regeneration of an existing role-restricted project.
findings.expected: R-073: "a generate request attributed to that project [from a Viewer is] refused ... while ... Editor ... succeed"; request: "Viewer: can open, copy, export and download only"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: reject "client-only checks without server enforcement." Project regeneration must enforce the current project's role server-side.
reproduction_steps: Open a project shared as Viewer and note that Synthesize is disabled.
Using an authorized API client, submit its regeneration request with that project's identity and previous output.
GenerateRequest ignores the project identity and starts a job for the Viewer.
The same request is never checked against the member's current Viewer role.
findings.evidence: server.py:77 configures extra='ignore'; GenerateRequest :79-95 has no project_id and generate_system :312 requires only current_user, not load_project(..., 'editor'). Workspace.jsx:213-221 sends a previous system without project identity; only the frontend readOnly flag at :161 and fieldsets prevent Viewer synthesis. In contrast projects.py:163 and :279-280 do check editor access for saves/uploads.

findings.title: Accepted long passwords ignore their suffix, so an old password can survive reset — bcrypt's 72-byte limit conflicts with the 128-character input contract
findings.surface: Email registration, sign-in and password reset with long/Unicode passwords
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two accepted passwords sharing the first 72 UTF-8 bytes but differing later authenticate as the same password. A user resetting an 80-character passphrase by changing its tail can still sign in with the old password, and Unicode passwords reach this byte boundary with fewer than 72 characters. The remaining prefix still supplies entropy, so the evidence supports a bounded password-identity failure rather than a general bypass. Users are not told to change the earlier prefix to recover.
findings.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "password hashing" and valid/wrong-password handling must preserve the supported password's identity; users rely on: "All characters of an accepted password determine whether it authenticates." For a reset, changing a supported password must invalidate the old distinct password, not ignore its suffix.
reproduction_steps: Register using a valid password longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes but within the 128-character limit.
Through a fresh reset link choose a different password with the same first 72 bytes and a changed suffix.
Sign out and try the old password.
bcrypt 4.1.3 ignores the differing suffix and accepts the old password too.

findings.title: Retrying a lost synthesis response spends credits twice — generation creation has no stable operation identity

findings.title: C++ code displays corrupted markup instead of clean highlighted code — regex passes rewrite their own HTML tags
